import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Quarter': ['Q1 2022', 'Q1 2022', 'Q1 2022', 'Q1 2022',
                'Q2 2022', 'Q2 2022', 'Q2 2022', 'Q2 2022',
                'Q3 2022', 'Q3 2022', 'Q3 2022', 'Q3 2022',
                'Q4 2022', 'Q4 2022', 'Q4 2022', 'Q4 2022',
                'Q1 2023', 'Q1 2023', 'Q1 2023', 'Q1 2023',
                'Q2 2023', 'Q2 2023', 'Q2 2023', 'Q2 2023',
                'Q3 2023', 'Q3 2023', 'Q3 2023', 'Q3 2023',
                'Q4 2023', 'Q4 2023', 'Q4 2023', 'Q4 2023'],
    'Service_Type': ['Pediatric', 'Adult', 'Geriatric', 'Maternity',
                     'Pediatric', 'Adult', 'Geriatric', 'Maternity',
                     'Pediatric', 'Adult', 'Geriatric', 'Maternity',
                     'Pediatric', 'Adult', 'Geriatric', 'Maternity',
                     'Pediatric', 'Adult', 'Geriatric', 'Maternity',
                     'Pediatric', 'Adult', 'Geriatric', 'Maternity',
                     'Pediatric', 'Adult', 'Geriatric', 'Maternity',
                     'Pediatric', 'Adult', 'Geriatric', 'Maternity'],
    'Patient_Volume': [1200, 2100, 1800, 950,
                       1350, 2250, 1950, 1050,
                       1280, 2150, 1880, 1020,
                       1400, 2350, 2100, 1150,
                       1380, 2280, 2000, 1100,
                       1500, 2400, 2150, 1200,
                       1450, 2300, 2050, 1180,
                       1600, 2500, 2280, 1300],
    'Utilization_Rate': [15.2, 32.5, 28.3, 22.1,
                         17.1, 34.2, 30.1, 24.3,
                         16.4, 33.0, 29.5, 23.8,
                         18.0, 36.2, 32.0, 26.0,
                         17.5, 35.8, 31.2, 25.5,
                         19.2, 37.5, 33.4, 27.2,
                         18.3, 34.8, 30.9, 24.8,
                         20.1, 38.3, 34.2, 28.5]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

quarter_order = ['Q1 2022', 'Q2 2022', 'Q3 2022', 'Q4 2022',
                 'Q1 2023', 'Q2 2023', 'Q3 2023', 'Q4 2023']
service_colors = {
    'Pediatric': '#4e79a7',
    'Adult': '#f28e2b',
    'Geriatric': '#e15759',
    'Maternity': '#76b7b2'
}

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

for service in df['Service_Type'].unique():
    subset = df[df['Service_Type'] == service]
    plt.scatter(subset['Patient_Volume'],
                subset['Utilization_Rate'],
                color=service_colors[service],
                label=service,
                s=100,
                alpha=0.8,
                edgecolors='w',
                linewidth=0.5)

plt.title('Healthcare Service Utilization Rate vs. Patient Volume by Demographic Group', fontsize=14, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Patient Volume', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Utilization Rate (%)', fontsize=12)
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png')

----
The chart presented is a scatter plot titled "Healthcare Service Utilization Rate vs. Patient Volume by Demographic Group." It visually explores the relationship between patient volume and healthcare service utilization rates across four distinct demographic service types: Pediatric, Adult, Geriatric, and Maternity.

The horizontal axis (x-axis) represents the patient volume, ranging from approximately 900 to 2,500 patients. The vertical axis (y-axis) displays the utilization rate as a percentage, spanning from 14% to 39%. Each data point on the scatter plot corresponds to a specific service type, differentiated by color: Pediatric services are shown in blue, Adult services in orange, Geriatric services in red, and Maternity services in teal.

From the image, several clusters and trends can be observed. Pediatric services, marked in blue, display lower utilization rates, generally between 15% and 20%, with patient volumes ranging from around 1,200 to 1,600. Adult services, represented in orange, show higher utilization rates, typically between 32% and 39%, and higher patient volumes, ranging from 2,100 to 2,500. Geriatric services, depicted in red, exhibit moderate to high utilization rates, mostly between 28% and 35%, with patient volumes between 1,800 and 2,300. Maternity services, shown in teal, have utilization rates varying from about 22% to 29%, and patient volumes from around 950 to 1,300.

The scatter plot effectively highlights the differences in healthcare service utilization among the various demographic groups, suggesting a positive correlation between patient volume and utilization rate, particularly pronounced in the Adult and Geriatric service categories. The grid lines in the background enhance readability, allowing for easier comparison of the data points.
